Equity Research 20 July 2026 | 5:01AM EDT
Ulta Beauty Inc. (ULTA)
Promotional event analysis, takeaways from IR call, and updating estimates
ULTA
12m Price Target: $648.00

We analyze traffic trends around Ulta's key promotional events. YTD, we have found that foot traffic accelerated for the Spring Haul and Big Summer Beauty Sale (2Q event). Web traffic has increased ~DD% for all events, which we find to be representative of Ulta's successful marketing strategies. We also discuss key takeaways from our recent conversation with IR at Ulta, including a growing focus on exclusivity, long term guidance, and the launch of TikTok Shop earlier in 2026.

Ulta continues to be heavily debated, as investors are concerned on the top line and SG&A expectations for the remainder of the year. Many question whether Ulta's 1Q strength is sustainable, noting the company faces its most difficult compare in 2Q, and the likely set up of decelerating SSS. Longer term, investors are increasingly highlighting risk around the beauty industry's increased points of distribution. However, we continue to reiterate our Buy on Ulta as we believe there could be upside to Ulta's SSS expectations given it is being fueled by a healthy cosmetics category, with the company's investment in marketing, labor, and service resulting in market share gains. Moreover, 2Q guidance appears relatively conservative, in our view, despite the tougher compare. We also highlight that Ulta's P/E multiple has lowered significantly to 15.8x vs. 1 year/3 year historicals of 19.5x/17.6x. We are increasing our 2Q comp estimate to reflect what we think are better trends in the quarter based on our work around the bigger promotion events and observed sales.
Traffic trends around promotional events

Management has consistently highlighted marketing as a key aspect of their growth strategy, noting that increased investments have led to higher traffic and guest conversion. Specifically, marketing investments include in-store events, creating exclusive collaborations with brand partners, accelerated digital and personalization efforts, and key promotional activation events.

Exhibit 7, highlighting that these events are a strong source of guest engagement and quarterly sales. We also analyze traffic YTD for these events, focusing on four events:

Jumbo Love and Love Your Skin event: Ulta's Jumbo Love and Love Your Skin events usually happen simultaneously and span a month. The sales start after the end of the winter holiday to the end of January. Jumbo Love features large discounts on premium hair care brands, while the Love Your Skin event provides up to \(50\%\) off on skincare brands. Management recently called out Jumbo Love and Love Your Skin as sources of their strong performance in 4Q25.

21 Days of Beauty: The 21 Days of Beauty event occurs in March and September every year, and features daily \(50 \%\)off promotions for a selection of skincare, haircare, makeup, and fragrance products. Management has stated that 21 Days of Beauty is a significant event that is used to determine customer preferences and marketing efficiency. In 3Q25, management attributed prestige makeup’s strength to 21 Days of Beauty, as brands such as Estee Lauder and MAC were standouts during the event. In 1Q26, management noted they had integrated marketplace brands into the event as well.

Spring Haul: Spring Haul is usually a ~10 day event in mid-April that features up to 30% off on select makeup, fragrance, hair care, and skincare. Management called out Spring Haul as a growth driver in 1Q26, and noted in 1Q25 that Spring Haul generated strong traffic and increases in member penetration.

Big Summer Beauty Sale: Big Summer Beauty Sale is a ~three week event in late June to mid July that offers up to 40% off and BOGO 50% off select brands. In 2Q25, management called out Big Summer Beauty Sale as a successful event, and noted that they had shifted promotional timing to better align with consumer behavior. In 2Q24, management noted that they had enhanced the event with a robust media strategy and engaging social content, which led to increased member reactivation and penetration of existing members.

When comparing the events this year to prior years, we found that foot traffic has accelerated for the Spring Haul and Big Summer Beauty Sale event. Web traffic also indicated ~DD% growth rates y/y for all events. We find these results to be representative of Ulta's effective promotional and go to market strategies.

Takeaways from our call with IR

Ulta is focused on driving a higher percent of exclusivity in its mix. In FY25, exclusive products comprised 11% of the company's assortment, up from 9% the prior year. Especially given the evolution of distribution in beauty, the company is thinking about how to further differentiate its assortment. Management is positive on the company's newness pipeline and feels good about the consistency, while explaining it will likely continue to evolve and look different in terms of the brands. We will likely see more smaller, emerging brands given there are not as many large brands Ulta does not already carry.

Long term guidance remains intact; \(12\%\) operating margin floor is no longer relevant. The company's long term algorithm includes top line sales growth in the \(+4 - 6\%\) range with operating profit growth in-line or better than that and +LDD EPS growth. When considering how to manage SG&A, management is focused on efficiency; the company plans to continue investing to gain share, but not at the elevated level from the last couple of years. At a recent conference, management explained that the \(12\%\) operating margin floor is no longer relevant as the company delivered \(12.4\%\) during an investment year in FY25.

Ulta launched its TikTok Shop in March. While this is not expected to be material for the year, management is pleased with the brant interest. Ulta's initial approach is to focus on exclusive brands. From a strategic standpoint, the goal is to get in front of a younger beauty enthusiast (i.e., member acquisition), as well as to use this as a brand-building lever. The company is looking to drive a more economic model through bundles vs. individual SKUs, with Ulta selling multi-branded bundles. Management explained that Ulta is one of the only retailers offering multi-branded bundles, which is a key opportunity for them. The company launched with 17 exclusive brands and 30 exclusive bundles.
Estimate Changes

We are increasing our 2Q comp growth estimate to +2.4% from +1.9% for what we think are better trends in the quarter based on our work around the bigger promotion events and observed sales. Additionally, we adjust our quarterly SG&A growth expectations. Our 2Q EBIT margin increases to 12.1% from 11.8%, and our 2Q EPS estimate increases to $6.19 from $6.02. Our FY26 comp growth estimate increases slightly to +3.4% from +3.3%, while our FY26 EBIT margin estimate remains consistent at 12.5%, and our FY26 EPS estimate increases to $28.95 from $28.80. Our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates increase by 0.5% to $32.37/$35.39, respectively.

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
